name: Mer
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Only survey wordlists exist (Peckham 1991; Starrenburg 1915); GlottologGlottolog's fullest description is only a wordlist. No grammar or phonology of Mer (Mairasi family, mnu) located.

sources.citation: Hays, Terence E. (comp.). n.d. [c.2003-2006]. West Papua (Irian Jaya) language bibliography, entry 'MER (Muri; Miere)'. Papuaweb (papuaweb.org/bib/hays/loc/), 3 pp.
sources.note: Bibliography only: every item listed for Mer is a survey/index/atlas mention (Silzer & Heikkinen 1984; Silzer & Clouse 1991; Peckham 1991b; Comrie 1992; Grimes 1992/1996/2000; Peters 1956 typescript; Capell 1954; Salzner 1960; Voorhoeve 1994; Galis 1955-56; Maurenbrecher 1953; Cowan 1953). No descriptive or phonological work exists in the list.

sources.citation: Badan Pengembangan dan Pembinaan Bahasa (Kemendikdasmen). Peta Bahasa: 'Bahasa Miere' (idb=644, Kampung Miere, Distrik Teluk Etna, Kab. Kaimana) and 'Bahasa Muri (Mer)' (idb=653, Kampung Wosimi, Distrik Naikere, Kab. Teluk Wondama). petabahasa.kemendikdasmen.go.id, accessed 2026-09-17.
sources.note: Location, speaker numbers (c.295 for Muri/Mer) and dialectometry percentages only; no phonology, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Hartzler, Margaret & LaLani Wood (eds.). 1991. Workpapers in Indonesian Languages and Cultures 10 - Irian Jaya. Abepura: UnCen-SIL. Full-volume scan 28 MB), SIL archives 93007.
sources.note: Completeness only: the two chapters that concern Mairasic (Mairasi phonology 111-145; Etna Bay survey 147-185) were obtained as separate chapter PDFs and read; the full volume would add nothing on Mer but would confirm no appendix was dropped from the chapter scans.

sources.citation: Peckham, Lloyd. 1991. Etna Bay survey report: Irian Jaya Bird's Neck languages. In Margaret Hartzler & LaLani Wood (eds.), Workpapers in Indonesian Languages and Cultures 10 (Irian Jaya), 147-185. Abepura: Cenderawasih University & Summer Institute of Linguistics. (SIL archives 37416; downloaded via Internet Archive copy of the SIL PDF)
sources.note: Nothing. Mer appears in the abstract (p.147), secs 3-3.1 (pp.148-151: 'Mer (Muri/Miere): Related to Semimi and Mairasi.. (200-400 people)') and a 209-item comparative Mairasi/Mer/Semimi wordlist (pp.173-179) transcribed without stress marks. The only phonological remarks (pp.152-153) concern Mairasi glottal stop vs Semimi /k/; no statement on stress/accent for Mer.

sources.citation: Peckham, Lloyd. 1991. Mairasi phonology. Workpapers in Indonesian Languages and Cultures 10: 111-145. Abepura: UnCen-SIL. (SIL archives 37613) -- sister language Mairasi [zrs, nucl1594], NOT Mer
sources.note: For Mairasi only (sec. 2.1, p.112): 'Primary stress (') is on the penultimate syllable. Secondary stress (") on words longer than three syllables occurs on the first syllable.' Also two contrastive pitch levels on stressed syllables (sec. 2.2.2). Mer is not mentioned anywhere in the chapter; kept for family context only.

sources.citation: Peckham, Nancy et al. [1991]. Farir Mairas Na'atuei / Perbendaharaan Kata Bahasa Mairasi / Mairasi Vocabulary. UnCen-SIL. (Rosetta Project excerpt, pronunciation page) -- sister language Mairasi
sources.note: Mairasi only: 'Word stress (accent) normally occurs on the next to the last syllable.' Nothing on Mer.
